# Design-space results (generated by studies/design_space_report.py; do not edit)

SKY130 room-temperature models. Reference point: s = 10 dec/V, 99.9 % (added 1 − F ≤ 1e-3), J + Stark, 50 ns adiabatic CZ. Every cell is used in charge-locked mode: half of C_node is the pulse capacitor (k ≈ 0.5).

## 1. Co-simulation: real waveforms on a multiplexed DAC line

Four cells on one line (10 pF), cell 0 pulsed through C_pulse, cell 1 refreshed at mid-gate (the line swings ~1.2 V during the gate), 1 µs from refresh to gate. In-situ calibration: the DAC code is corrected with a linear fit of the settled level, and the CZ amplitude with the coupling k measured at the electrode's own bias. *Global k*: one k, calibrated at 0.9 V, for all electrodes. Droop is not included in this table (see section 2).

## 2. How the error terms combine (real waveform with a droop offset added)

Each co-simulated point gets a droop offset of ±½ and ±1 × the static budget left. The real infidelity is compared with three rules. *Independent*: infidelities add (the rule for independent random errors). *Coherent*: static offsets add as voltages, and the dynamic part adds in infidelity. *Phase-additive*: every deterministic term adds in the adiabatic phases (linearised), then 1 − F follows from the phases.

| rule | median \|rule / real − 1\| | max | points |
|---|---|---|---|
| independent | 0.0659 | 55.1 | 240 |
| coherent | 0.0283 | 56.8 | 240 |
| phase-additive | 0.0013 | 0.132 | 240 |

## 5. Design grid

900 points (0 failed): W × C_node × ESD × (underdrive 0 / 0.3 V, or buffer current 1 / 10 nA for TSWO). Hold time = droop budget / droop, with the droop budget = static allowance (after the pulse distortion) − ε (10 % of the spec, settling) − |residual pedestal|, doubled by centring. Electrodes per line: n · t_slot(n) ≤ hold time, flat 50 Ω line (10 pF wire + n off switches) or a tree demux (line fixed at 10 pF + 1000 switches). Power per electrode: refresh energy (clock + 1000-electrode line share + top-up) / hold time, plus static: the OTA buffer's measured supply power for TSWO, and the same (1.7 nW, TSWO at 1 nA) for the ideal-buffer designs TSWB and NTB.
